Title: Fetch tickets by status using natural language query
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running on localhost:8000 | 2. JIRA credentials configured in .env | 3. JIRA instance has tickets with 'In Progress' status
Steps: 1. Start backend server: python backend/main.py | 2. Open Streamlit UI: streamlit run ui/app.py | 3. Navigate to 'Natural Language Query' tab | 4. Enter query: "Fetch the descriptions and IDs of all tickets with status 'in progress'" | 5. Click 'Submit Query' button | 6. Observe response
Test Data: Query: "Fetch the descriptions and IDs of all tickets with status 'in progress'"
Expected Result: System returns list of tickets with status 'In Progress' showing ticket keys (IDs) and descriptions. Each ticket displays: key (e.g. PROJ-123)

Title: Fetch tickets using status-based search
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Tickets exist with 'Done' status
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Status-Based Search' tab | 3. Enter status: "Done" | 4. Set max results slider to 20 | 5. Click 'Fetch Tickets' button | 6. Review displayed tickets
Expected Result: System displays up to 20 tickets with 'Done' status. Each ticket card shows: key in blue, summary, status, assignee, and first 200 characters of description. Success message shows count: "Found X ticket(s)"

Title: Get details of specific ticket
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Valid ticket key exists (e.g., PROJ-123)
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Ticket Details' tab | 3. Enter ticket key: "PROJ-123" | 4. Click 'Get Details' button | 5. Verify all fields displayed
Expected Result: System displays complete ticket information in two columns: Basic Information (Key, Summary, Status, Type) and Assignment & Dates (Assignee, Reporter, Priority, Created, Updated). Full description shown below in separate section. Success message: "Ticket found: PROJ-123"

Title: Complete workflow from backend API to UI display
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Multiple tickets exist with various statuses
Steps: 1. Start backend: python backend/main.py | 2. Verify health endpoint: curl http://localhost:8000/health | 3. Test API directly: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/jira/status -d '{"status":"In Progress"}' | 4. Start UI: streamlit run ui/app.py | 5. Use UI to fetch same tickets | 6. Compare API response with UI display
Expected Result: Backend health check returns status:healthy. API returns JSON with tickets array. UI displays same tickets in formatted cards. Ticket counts match between API response and UI display. All ticket fields (key, summary, status, assignee, description) correctly propagate from backend to UI.

Title: Search tickets using JQL query
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Tickets exist with High priority and In Progress status
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'JQL Query' tab | 3. Enter JQL: "status = \"In Progress\" AND priority = High" | 4. Set max results to 30 | 5. Click 'Execute Query' button | 6. Verify results match JQL criteria
Test Data: JQL: "status = \"In Progress\" AND priority = High", Max Results: 30
Expected Result: System executes JQL query and returns matching tickets. All returned tickets have status='In Progress' AND priority='High'. Ticket cards display key, summary, status, and priority. Success message shows count. If no matches, info message: "No tickets found matching the JQL query."

Title: Query for non-existent ticket key
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Ticket key NONEXIST-99999 does not exist in JIRA
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Ticket Details' tab | 3. Enter ticket key: "NONEXIST-99999" | 4. Click 'Get Details' button | 5. Observe error handling
Expected Result: System displays error message in red: "Error: [detail]" or "Ticket not found". No partial data shown. UI remains functional and user can enter different ticket key. Backend returns 404 status code.

Title: Fetch tickets with status that has no matches
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. No tickets exist with status 'Obsolete'
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Status-Based Search' tab | 3. Enter status: "Obsolete" | 4. Click 'Fetch Tickets' button | 5. Observe response
Expected Result: System returns success with count of 0. Info message displays: "No tickets found with the specified criteria." No error thrown. UI shows empty results area. User can immediately try different status without page reload.

Title: Execute invalid JQL query
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'JQL Query' tab | 3. Enter invalid JQL: "invalid syntax here @#$" | 4. Click 'Execute Query' button | 5. Observe error handling
Expected Result: System displays error message explaining JQL syntax error. Error returned from JIRA API is shown to user. Red error message appears in UI. No partial results displayed. User can correct JQL and retry without refreshing page.

Title: Handle very long ticket descriptions
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Ticket exists with description exceeding 1000 characters
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Ticket Details' tab | 3. Enter ticket key of ticket with long description | 4. Click 'Get Details' button | 5. Verify description display | 6. Also test same ticket in Status-Based Search
Expected Result: In Ticket Details view: Full description displayed under Description section. In Status-Based Search view: Description truncated to 200 characters with ellipsis (...). No layout breaking. Scroll available for long text. All other fields display correctly alongside long description.

Title: Maximum results boundary test
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. JIRA instance has > 100 tickets with 'In Progress' status
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Status-Based Search' tab | 3. Set max results slider to 100 (maximum) | 4. Enter status with many matches | 5. Click 'Fetch Tickets' button | 6. Verify result count and performance
Expected Result: System returns exactly 100 tickets even if more exist in JIRA. Success message shows: "Found 100 ticket(s)". All 100 tickets render correctly in UI. Page remains responsive. Backend respects maxResults parameter. No timeout errors. Load time acceptable (<5 seconds).

Title: Backend health check endpoint
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running on localhost:8000
Steps: 1. Open browser or use curl | 2. Navigate to: http://localhost:8000/health | 3. Observe response
Expected Result: Returns JSON: {"status": "healthy", "jira_tool_initialized": true/false, "jira_agent_initialized": true/false}. HTTP status code 200. Response indicates whether JIRA components initialized successfully based on .env configuration.

Title: Search tickets by keyword
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Tickets exist containing word 'authentication'
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Text Search' tab | 3. Enter search text: "authentication" | 4. Set max results to 25 | 5. Click 'Search' button | 6. Review results
Expected Result: System returns tickets where 'authentication' appears in summary or description. Results show up to 25 matching tickets. Each ticket card displays: key, summary, status, assignee, and description snippet. Success message shows count: "Found X ticket(s)". Search is case-insensitive.

Title: API documentation accessibility
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running on localhost:8000
Steps: 1. Open browser | 2. Navigate to: http://localhost:8000/docs | 3. Explore interactive API documentation | 4. Test an endpoint using 'Try it out' feature
Test Data: Example: Test /health endpoint from docs UI
Expected Result: Interactive Swagger/OpenAPI documentation loads. All endpoints listed: /, /jira/query, /jira/status, /jira/ticket/{key}, /jira/search, /jira/jql, /health. Each endpoint shows request models, response models, and example values. 'Try it out' feature allows testing endpoints directly from docs. Responses appear inline.

Title: Backend handles missing JIRA credentials gracefully
Preconditions: 1. Backend server starting | 2. .env file has placeholder values or missing JIRA credentials | 3. JIRA_SERVER, JIRA_EMAIL, or JIRA_API_TOKEN not set or invalid
Steps: 1. Ensure .env has placeholder credentials | 2. Start backend: python backend/main.py | 3. Observe startup logs | 4. Make request to /jira/status endpoint | 5. Check response
Expected Result: Backend starts successfully with warning message in console: "JIRA initialization failed: [error details]". Server remains running. Endpoints return 503 status with message: "JIRA tool not initialized. Check JIRA credentials in .env file." Health endpoint shows jira_tool_initialized: false. No crash or unhandled exception.

Title: Submit empty natural language query
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Streamlit UI open
Steps: 1. Navigate to 'Natural Language Query' tab | 2. Leave query input field empty | 3. Click 'Submit Query' button | 4. Observe validation
Expected Result: UI displays warning message: "Please enter a query." Warning appears in yellow/orange. No API request sent to backend. Input field remains focused for user to enter query. No error logged on backend.

Title: Submit empty status in status-based search
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Streamlit UI open
Steps: 1. Navigate to 'Status-Based Search' tab | 2. Leave status field empty | 3. Click 'Fetch Tickets' button | 4. Observe validation
Expected Result: UI displays warning message: "Please enter a status." Warning appears in yellow/orange. No API request sent to backend. User prompted to enter status before proceeding. Form remains in editable state.

Title: Backend unavailable when UI tries to connect
Preconditions: 1. Backend server is NOT running | 2. Streamlit UI is running
Steps: 1. Start only Streamlit UI: streamlit run ui/app.py | 2. Observe health check result in UI | 3. Try to submit any query
Expected Result: UI detects backend is unavailable. Red error message appears: "Backend service is not running. Please start the backend server first." Info message shows command: "Run: python backend/main.py or uvicorn backend.main:app --reload". All query forms hidden/disabled. User cannot proceed until backend is started.

Title: Invalid ticket key format
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Streamlit UI open
Steps: 1. Navigate to 'Ticket Details' tab | 2. Enter invalid format: "not-a-valid-key" | 3. Click 'Get Details' button | 4. Observe error
Expected Result: Backend attempts to fetch ticket and JIRA returns error. UI displays error message in red showing JIRA's response. User informed ticket doesn't exist or format invalid. User can correct input and retry. No application crash.

Title: Project filter with non-existent project key
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Project key FAKE does not exist
Steps: 1. Open Streamlit UI | 2. Navigate to 'Status-Based Search' tab | 3. Enter status: "In Progress" | 4. Enter project: "FAKE" | 5. Click 'Fetch Tickets' button | 6. Observe result
Expected Result: System executes query and returns 0 results. Info message: "No tickets found with the specified criteria." No error thrown since query is valid but returns empty set. User can modify project key and retry.

Title: Concurrent UI requests to backend
Preconditions: 1. Backend server running | 2. JIRA credentials configured | 3. Two browser tabs with UI open
Steps: 1. Open two browser tabs with Streamlit UI | 2. In tab 1: Start a status search for "In Progress" | 3. Immediately in tab 2: Start JQL query | 4. Observe both requests complete | 5. Check backend logs
Test Data: Tab 1: Status "In Progress" | Tab 2: JQL query
Expected Result: Both requests processed by backend concurrently. Both UI tabs receive responses. No request blocking or timeout. Backend remains stable. Responses are independent and correct for each request. No cross-request data contamination.
